incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: reserved-gpu-pool-3 saturation detected for zone-us-east-1. queue_depth=142, throttled_requests=38, affected_tenants=[AcmeCorp]. detected at 2035012345
Alex P: seeing it, thanks. is this autoscaler failing to add nodes or are we hitting pool limits?
Sanjay K: quick look at autoscaler logs shows many scale requests rejected. error: "scale request denied: pool_max_capacity_reached"
Maria L: AcmeCorp has a large reserved commit on pool-3 but we also have several non-reserved jobs pinned there. could be noisy customer consuming all reserved GPUs.
Cheng W: I'm on on-call. tagging @oncall-bot to take handoff.
oncall-bot: @Cheng W you are now on-call for this incident. priority: P1. please coordinate mitigations.
Cheng W: got it. first actions: 1) pause non-critical preemptible jobs in pool-3 2) attempt transient shard evictions 3) notify customer support and impacted tenant.
Zara T: pausing preemptible queue now: `./runctl queue pause --pool pool-3 --label preemptible`
Alex P: good. also lets check if autoscaler config has a hard cap. `kubectl get cm autoscaler-config -n runtime -o yaml`
Sanjay K: snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:05:12Z scale_request: pool=pool-3 desired=18 current=12
2026-03-15T02:05:12Z response: rejected code=PoolMaxReached limit=12
```
Maria L: that limit=12 is the reserved cap for pool-3 (contractual). we can't auto-provision beyond that without violating tenancy.
Cheng W: so autoscaler is working but contract cap is hit. mitigation options: - evict noisy tenant containers not in AcmeCorp reserved slice - shift some AcmeCorp traffic to hosted fallback models (if permitted) - open emergency temporary overprovision change with commercial
Alex P: can we measure which tenants are using which GPUs? `gpu-mapper --pool pool-3 --report` returns per-tenant allocation.
Sanjay K: ran it. output top lines:
```
pool-3 allocations:
AcmeCorp: 9 gpus (reserved slice)
TenantX: 6 gpus (non-reserved)
MLBench: 3 gpus (short jobs)
```
Zara T: TenantX looks like the noisy one. those jobs are long-running experiments from a partner.
Cheng W: actioning eviction of non-reserved infra: `scheduler evict --pool pool-3 --tenant TenantX --grace 60s`
Alex P: please be careful—eviction of customer jobs is risky. get approval from ops-lead?
Cheng W: I called ops-lead and got verbal sign-off for emergency preemption. proceeding.
Maria L: support-bot notify AcmeCorp of degraded performance and that we're applying mitigations.
support-bot: @AcmeCorp Support: We are seeing degraded throughput on reserved GPUs in us-east-1. Actions: evict noisy non-reserved jobs, shift traffic to hosted fallback. ETA for initial improvements ~ 7-12 minutes. (incident id: 2035012345)

Sanjay K: eviction completed, reclaiming 6 gpus from TenantX. current allocations: AcmeCorp=9, reclaimed=6, available=6
Alex P: autoscaler now able to rebalance internal slots, but still can't exceed contractual limit for pool-3. recommend using routing policy to divert overflow to dedicated-spare or hosted-api.
Cheng W: applying routing override: `route-policy set --pool pool-3 --overflow=hosted-fallback --percent=40`
Maria L: route changes applied. initial traffic reroute shows drop in queue_depth from 142 -> 64 within 90s. :thumbsup:
Zara T: monitoring latencies on AcmeCorp requests — p95 spiked to 3.2s but now trending down to 1.1s.
Alex P: also enabling temporary token-level throttling for low-priority endpoints for AcmeCorp to reduce token churn. `throttle set --tenant AcmeCorp --policy conservative`
Cheng W: pinging commercial to request emergency capacity increase for pool-3 to fulfill SLA. created slack thread with SRE-commercial.
Maria L: good. also create incident ticket for billing/contract: `INC-2035` and tag account execs.
Sanjay K: quick root-cause hypothesis: a partner (TenantX) had an automated onboarding job that scaled up and pinned GPUs into pool-3 which is the same physical pool as AcmeCorp reserved slice. autoscaler respected contractual cap and rejected scale beyond. combined with no preemptible eviction, queue built up and customer saw throttles.
Cheng W: current status: queue_depth=18, throttled_requests=2, AcmeCorp p95 latency=0.9s. reclaimed resources stable.
Alex P: next steps: 1) followup to ensure noisy tenant has backoff configured 2) add preemptible eviction policy to run automatically when reserved tenants are impacted 3) explore routing overflow by default for reserved slices when pool at cap.
Zara T: I'm taking action item to add an alert rule that correlates reserved_usage_ratio > 0.9 and queue_growth > 20 in 5m.
Maria L: on customer comms: support-bot sent customer note and follow-up email template. please update once commercial confirms capacity increase.
Sanjay K: logging note for postmortem: `scale request denied` + `tenantX pinned` + `eviction performed` + `40% overflow routing enacted`
Cheng W: handing back to runbook. putting summary in incidents channel. I'll keep monitoring for next 30m.
oncall-bot: @Cheng W incident auto-escalation timer set for 30 minutes. please update status or escalate.
Alex P: thanks team. will file postmortem and link to this thread.
Maria L: action items assigned: Zara - alert rule; Alex - postmortem draft; Sanjay - autoscaler config review; Cheng - follow-up with commercial + customer update.
support-bot: Customer impact resolved for now. marking incident as mitigated but still investigating.
Cheng W: closing thread summary: mitigated by evicting noisy tenant, enabling overflow routing to hosted fallback, applying temporary throttles, notifying AcmeCorp. follow-up: contractual review and automation to prevent recurrence. :white_check_mark:
